name: Bughotu
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Ivens, W. G. 1933. A grammar of the language of Bugotu, Ysabel Island, Solomon Islands. Bulletin of the School of Oriental Studies 7(1): 141-177 (primary; p.142 read from page scan, archive.org;ernet.dli.2015.70631 leaf 160; scanned of both archive.org copies…
catalog_locator: Ivens 1933 p.142 ('Accent'); Codrington 1885 p.546 (Bugotu intro) and p.523 (Florida intro, sentence immediately before 'I. Alphabet')
catalog_quote: Ivens 1933 p.142: "Accent.—The accent in Bugotu is generally on the antep...mate syllable : suli, suīsuli." [the right margin of p.142 is a torn strip re-pasted one line high in both archive.org copies; 'antep' and 'mate' are legible either side of it, i.e. 'antepenultimate'; a diacritic sits on the first syllable(s) of the reduplicated example but is not cleanly legible]. Codrington 1885 p.546: "Phonologically the two languages [Bugotu and Florida] do not differ much, though the presence of f, j, gn, in Bugotu materially affects the sound, and dh stands for l instead of h. Bugotu also has the singular characteristic of throwing the accent backwards to the antepenultimate, though by no means as a rule." Codrington 1885 p.523 (Florida): "The accent of words is generally on the penultimate syllable."

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three deciding quotations are verbatim in copies we hold at the stated places (Ivens p.142 page scan with the disclosed torn margin; Codrington p.546 and p.523 in the djvu text). A clean third scan of BSOS 7 (archive.org dli.calcutta.05222, leaf 146) downloaded now reads 'generally on the antepenultimate syllable : suli, suīsuli' in full, so the reading is no longer inferential; the record's bracketed caveat can be replaced by a citation of this scan (files under, record). (2) Deciding source is a 1933 36-page missionary grammar sketch, corroborated by Codrington 1885; Glottolog lists no other grammar/phonology and web search found no modern phonological, instrumental or dissertation treatment of Bughotu stress, so this is very probably the best available published description.
